column7: TRIGGER-ROWDIGEST-1 (docs/design/trigger-rowdigest.md). The per-statement generation proof checks only that both triggers exist and are ENABLE ALWAYS, so the owner of the trigger function (the server database role, no superuser needed) could replace its body with one that bumps nothing, re-create a trigger of the same name on fewer events, or DISABLE/write/ENABLE ALWAYS inside one transaction, and a permission later removed by direct SQL kept authorizing from every warm replica until restart. A periodic check (role_permission_generation_integrity.go) now compares the function body, settings and trigger definition with this release and the catalog rows xmin with the last reading; on a difference it logs, counts keyorix_role_permission_generation_tamper_total, re-installs and bumps the generation, which invalidates every replica cache. Also _DisableWriteEnableInOneTransactionIsFlushed_Postgres, _ReplaceThenRestoreIsFlushed_Postgres, _TriggerRecreatedOnFewerEventsIsRestored_Postgres, _FunctionSettingsAreRestored_Postgres, _CleanTicksAndReplicaBootsDoNotFlush_Postgres, _BackgroundJobFlushesAndStopsOnClose_Postgres; installer half TestRolePermissionGeneration_EnsureLeavesCorrectFunctionRowAlone_Postgres and _EnsureRestoresRecreatedTrigger_Postgres (both red on main by behaviour). Residual: one interval for deliberate DDL; a superuser below SQL is not detected.
